title: A local model button on the first-run sign-in screen — the mockups, round 4

steps.path: The screen a new install shows before the app opens
steps.headline: Every way in is the same outlined button, including Use a local model and Use an API key.
steps.changed: Log in with Claude is no longer filled, Use an API key became a button, and Use a local model was added (Q-1).
steps.notice: All five buttons look alike and light up on hover. The card is two buttons taller than today.

steps.path: After pressing Use a local model
steps.headline: Local setup suggests one model, shown with the same row as Settings, Local models.
steps.changed: The suggestion is the Local models row itself: size, fit line and its Download button (your round 3 notes).
steps.notice: Choose a different model, Use an app on this computer and Back sit below it.

steps.path: Local setup, after pressing Choose a different model
steps.headline: Choose a different model opens the same search and list as Settings, Local models.
steps.changed: It is that screen's Models card, not a copy, so the two can never differ (B-3).
steps.notice: A new install sees only Recommended; the installed rows here are sample data.

steps.path: Local setup, on a computer with little memory
steps.headline: On a small computer the warning uses the Local models amber, on the line and on the model's fit.
steps.changed: The boxed amber note is gone; the warning is amber text like a tight fit in Settings (B-4).
steps.notice: The row itself reads "Will be tight — close other apps first".

steps.path: Local setup, after pressing Use an app on this computer
steps.headline: Model apps already running on this computer each get a Connect button, with how many models they have.
steps.changed: Setup looks for running model apps and connects to one instead of downloading.
steps.notice: Pressing one finishes setup on that app's models.
steps.risk: Only Ollama and LM Studio are found automatically today.

steps.path: Use an app on this computer, when nothing is found
steps.headline: With nothing found, it just asks: Enter the address for your local endpoint.
steps.changed: No "none found" line and no "or enter" framing (C-13).
steps.notice: Check again looks for running apps again.

steps.path: The band above the message box, right after setup
steps.headline: While setup's first model downloads, a band above the message box shows its progress and time left.
steps.changed: Only when nothing else can answer yet (B-5); later downloads are never announced here.
steps.notice: It says plainly that the assistant can answer once the download is done.
steps.risk: The preview shows the band in every chat.

steps.path: The band above the message box, after quitting mid-download
steps.headline: If setup closed before that first download finished, the band says so and offers Resume download.
steps.changed: Same rule as the downloading band: only when the app has nothing else to answer with (B-6).
steps.notice: One button picks the download back up where it stopped.

steps.path: After pressing Use an API key
steps.headline: Use an API key opens its own page, like Use a local model, and names whose key you pasted.
steps.changed: The key box moved off the sign-in card onto its own page with Back to sign-in (A-7).
steps.notice: Pasting an OpenAI key shows "OpenAI key" before Verify & Continue.

steps.path: The API key page, pasting a key the app cannot place
steps.headline: A key the app cannot place asks "Which service is this key for?" with a dropdown.
steps.changed: Only an unusual key gets the extra question (F-1).
steps.notice: Verify & Continue stays off until a service is known.

steps.path: After pressing Log in with Claude
steps.headline: Log in with Claude installs Claude Code first, shown once on the card, then the browser opens.
steps.changed: The checklist above no longer repeats the install (B-9).
steps.notice: The sign-in follows on its own once the install finishes.

steps.path: Settings, Assistant settings, Cloud providers, the Claude Code card
steps.headline: Without Claude Code, its card offers Install Claude Code instead of telling you to restart.
steps.changed: "Restart YouCoded to run setup again" is replaced by an Install button (F-5).
steps.notice: One press installs it right here, ready for the Claude sign-in.

steps.path: The model chip in the bottom strip, a greyed Claude model
steps.headline: Greyed Claude models say "Install Claude Code" and open the card that installs it.
steps.changed: The greyed row's reason becomes a link to the Claude Code card (F-5).
steps.notice: Picking a Claude model without Claude Code is one click away from fixing it.
